punctilious

punk-TIL-ee-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Punctilious is showing extreme, precise attention to detail and correct procedure.

The wedding planner was punctilious about every detail, measuring the exact distance between each place setting twice.

Example

The auditor's punctilious review caught a rounding error that three previous reviewers had missed entirely.

Catching a rounding error that three other reviewers missed is exactly the exacting precision punctilious describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

meticulous: Meticulous (taught earlier in this course) means showing great care and precision about details of any kind -- a lab notebook, a packing list. Punctilious narrows that care to correct procedure and formal conduct: protocol, etiquette, the proper order of steps, observed to the letter.

scrupulous: Scrupulous means exact and principled -- attentive to detail because honesty and conscience demand it, as in a scrupulous accounting of every donated dollar. Punctilious cares less about conscience and more about form: it follows rules of procedure and etiquette precisely, whatever the motive.

ceremonious: Ceremonious means marked by ceremony and formal pomp -- bows, titles, ritual courtesies performed at full length. Punctilious is about exactness rather than display: every rule of procedure or etiquette followed to the letter, with or without any pomp at all.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

slapdash: done hastily and carelessly

Where it sits · how exacting the precision is — careful → punctilious → obsessive

careful vs. punctilious: Careful describes ordinary attentiveness that most tasks require; punctilious describes a much more formal, almost ceremonial precision about procedure.

obsessive vs. punctilious: Obsessive pushes past punctilious into precision without a purpose: punctilious care still serves correct procedure, while obsessive checking is repeated past all reason, long after the task is done.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — punctil

root — punctil: small point (Latin/Italian (punctum, punctiglio))

suffix — -ious

suffix — -ious: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Punctilious comes from Latin punctum ('point') by way of Italian punctiglio ('a fine point of conduct') + -ious -- literally 'attentive to fine points.'

Use the root in a new word: puncture

Use the root in a new word: puncture: The same punctum root gives us the everyday word puncture, a small hole made by a sharp point -- the same 'sharp point' image behind punctilious's exacting attention to detail.

Word Choice

Punctilious is closely related to "meticulous" (taught earlier in this course): meticulous describes thoroughness about details generally, while punctilious adds a specific formality -- following rules of conduct or procedure to the letter, almost like etiquette.
